hints: Use the gap method: first arrange the 5 men in a line in $5!$ ways.
The 5 men create 6 possible spaces (gaps), including the two ends, where a woman can stand.
Choose and arrange 2 of these 6 gaps for the 2 women using ${}^6\mathrm{P}_2$.
walkthrough:
Arrange the 5 men in a line first:
$$\text{Ways to arrange men} = 5! = 120$$

The 5 men create 6 available spaces (including the ends) where women can be placed so that no two women are adjacent:
$$\_ M_1 \_ M_2 \_ M_3 \_ M_4 \_ M_5 \_$$

Place the 2 women into 2 of these 6 distinct spaces:
$$\text{Ways to place women} = {}^{6}\mathrm{P}_2 = 6 \times 5 = 30$$

Multiply the two results:
$$\text{Total arrangements} = 5! \times {}^{6}\mathrm{P}_2 = 120 \times 30 = 3600\text{ ways}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Method 1: The Gap Method (Recommended)
Step 1: Arrange the unrestricted items first.
There are $5$ men. The number of ways to arrange the $5$ men in a row is:
$$5! = 5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 120$$

Step 2: Identify the available gaps.
Placing the $5$ men creates $6$ available slots (gaps) where a woman could stand without being next to another woman:
$$\_ M \_ M \_ M \_ M \_ M \_$$

Step 3: Place the $2$ women into these $6$ gaps.
Because the two women are distinct individuals, order matters:
$${}^{6}\mathrm{P}_2 = \frac{6!}{(6 - 2)!} = 6 \times 5 = 30$$

Step 4: Multiply by the fundamental counting principle:
$$\text{Total ways} = 120 \times 30 = 3600$$

Method 2: Subtraction Method (Complement)
Step 1: Total unrestricted arrangements of all $7$ people ($5$ men and $2$ women):
$$7! = 5040$$

Step 2: Arrangements where the $2$ women stand next to each other.
Treat the $2$ women as a single unit $(W_1 W_2)$:
- Number of entities to arrange: $5$ men $+ 1$ block $= 6$ entities $\implies 6! = 720$
- Internal arrangement of the $2$ women within the block: $2! = 2$
$$\text{Ways with women together} = 6! \times 2! = 720 \times 2 = 1440$$

Step 3: Subtract from total:
$$\text{Ways with women not together} = 5040 - 1440 = 3600$$
